title: Pimento cheese
subtitle: Southern cheddar, cream cheese, and pimento spread
excerpt: Pimento cheese is a thick, spreadable mixture of grated cheddar, cream cheese, mayonnaise, and jarred pimento peppers, seasoned with cayenne and onion powder. It is a staple of the American South, spread on white bread for sandwiches, served with crackers, or used as a dip. Takes five minutes to make.
sourceNotes: Southern American culinary tradition. Pimento cheese is documented in Southern cookery writing from the early twentieth century and is a fixture of Southern entertaining and everyday eating. Edna Lewis, The Taste of Country Cooking (1976), references it as a childhood staple.

recipe.yieldDescription: About 400 g spread (serves 8 to 10 as a starter or snack)
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Better made the day before to let the flavours come together. Keeps refrigerated for up to 5 days.

content.text: Pimento cheese is grated cheddar and cream cheese mashed together with mayonnaise, diced pimento peppers, cayenne, and onion powder. It is a cold spread that works on white bread, crackers, or celery sticks. The key is using a sharp, mature cheddar: it gives the flavour the spread lives by.

items.prepNote: 2 tbsp jarred pimento or roasted red pepper, drained and finely diced

content.text: Combine {{cheddar}} of coarsely grated mature cheddar, {{cream-cheese}} of cream cheese, {{mayonnaise}} of mayonnaise, the drained diced pimento or roasted red pepper, the cayenne, onion powder, salt, and black pepper in a bowl. Mash and stir until evenly combined but not completely smooth: some texture is part of the appeal. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving. The spread firms as it chills and the flavours develop.

items.cause: Not enough mayonnaise or cream cheese too cold.
items.fix: Add another tablespoon of mayonnaise and stir well. Make sure the cream cheese is at room temperature before mixing.
Drain the pimento well and pat dry with kitchen paper before chopping.

content.text: Adding a finely chopped jalapeño gives heat. A tablespoon of grated onion in place of onion powder is the traditional Southern version. Some recipes add a teaspoon of Dijon mustard for sharpness. Grilled pimento cheese sandwiches, cooked in the same way as a grilled cheese, are the classic hot application.

Pimento cheese is the official sandwich spread of the American South, so woven into the culture that it is called 'the caviar of the South'. It appears on the Masters golf tournament menu at Augusta National every year, at church suppers, debutante parties, and on white-bread sandwiches in children's lunchboxes. It is not common outside the South and is not well understood by non-Southerners until they taste it.
